entities.summary: William Stewart MacMillan was a Canadian hockey coach and player. MacMillan played and later coached in the National Hockey League (NHL). After several years with the Canada national team, including playing at two World Championships and the 1968 Winter Olympics, winning a bronze medal, MacMillan made his NHL debut in 1970 with the Toronto Maple Leafs. He played for Toronto, the Atlanta Flames, and New York Islanders between 1970 and 1977, and retired from playing in 1978. He became a coach during his final year, spent in the minor CHL and moved to the NHL in 1979 when he became an assistant coach for the Islanders.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: MacMillan played for Toronto, Atlanta Flames, and New York Islanders between 1970 and 1977, contributing to the team's success during his playing career. As an assistant coach for the Islanders in 1979, he helped shape their future.
